notes.1a: This was well answered with most candidates correctly calculating the percentage of factory profit used by the company.
notes.1b: The manufacturing account was prepared without any errors by well-prepared candidates.
notes.1c: The income statement was prepared to a high standard. The most common error was the omission of the decrease in provision for unrealised profit. Some candidates used unacceptable labels and were not awarded marks.
notes.1d: Although most candidates did provide the required advice the justification was often limited.
notes.1e: Nearly all candidates stated the meaning of prime cost and were able to provide the two required examples.
notes.2a: Very few candidates were able to state three advantages but nearly all did receive some credit.
notes.2b: The depreciation calculations were well answered with most candidates calculating the depreciation on the buildings correctly. Many did also make the other two calculations correctly but being more complex there were some errors which appeared to be careless rather than demonstrating a lack of knowledge and understanding.
notes.2c: The note was also well prepared and the layout and presentation were good in most instances.
notes.2d: Nearly all candidates recommended an option and gave relevant justification for the recommendation.
notes.3a: Most candidates were able to calculate the profit correctly and gained full marks. There were no common errors but a limited few did omit one of the transactions.
notes.3b: The joint venture accounts were prepared to a high standard with few errors.
notes.3c: Most candidates were able to identify and then develop a benefit of setting up a joint venture.
notes.3d: Nearly all candidates made a recommendation but the justification was often generic rather than specific to the given scenario. �PAGE�22
notes.4a: Nearly all candidates gave an acceptable explanation of the difference between a bonus issue and a rights issue with many being awarded all three available marks.
notes.4b: The profit calculation was made correctly by many candidates. The most common error was the miscalculation of the finance costs which related to interest charges for six months only.
notes.4c: The statement of changes in equity was prepared to a high standard. A few candidates incorrectly included the final proposed dividend in the statement.
notes.4d: The statement of financial position was also prepared to a high standard with many fully correct statements and no common errors.
notes.5a: Although many candidates did identify two advantages many did not develop the advantage sufficiently to gain the second mark for each advantage.
notes.5b: This was very well answered with most candidates producing a fully correct flexed budget and there were no common errors.
notes.5c: Most candidates were able to explain possible reasons for the difference between the flexed budget and the actual data.
notes.5d: This was not so well answered with relatively few identifying the difficulty in evaluating performance if a fixed budget is produced.
notes.6a: Nearly all candidates calculated the required annual net cash flow correctly. Where there were errors these appeared to be due to inattention rather than lack of understanding.
notes.6b: Although many candidates did calculate the accounting rate of return correctly a significant number did not account for the depreciation of the machinery.
notes.6c: Many candidates correctly calculated the ARR for Option 2 but again some candidates did not account for depreciation.
notes.6d: Nearly all candidates were aware of the advantages and disadvantages of ARR as a method of investment appraisal.
notes.6e: Many candidates did not address the non-financial factors and generally only provided two appropriate points.
notes.general_comments: Overall performance of candidates was good with many candidates achieving a high grade.
